text.p: - The newly created Temporary Emergency Tax Commission was intended by Russian authorities as a desperate effort to demonstrate that power in the country is still active.
- Despite the lack of centralised administrative power in the Chechen capital Grozny, life there is slowly coming back to normal.
- According to Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits, the budget deficit for 1997 will remain unchanged and tax privileges for a number of enterprises will be cut down.

- The decision to freeze Russia's participation in the division of the Black Sea Fleet passed yesterday by the State Duma lower house of the Russian parliament is likely to have a negative impact on the meeting of the Russian and Ukrainian presidents which is due to take place in Moscow today.

- Introducing the idea of "tough state control" over tax policy, Russian authorities -- namely Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and the president's chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais -- propose to revise the present economic course, the paper says.
Results of the regional elections in Russia may lead to a significant change in relations between central and local powers in the country.
- The big personnel reshuffle in the Kremlin cannot solve serious problems caused by the looming political crisis in the country.
- An opinion poll conducted by the paper's sociological centre in the Tula region of Central Russia shows the province is longing for a military dictatorship.
